nodes.question: How was the DEET stock solution prepared for the study?
nodes.answer: The DEET stock solution was prepared by dissolving 0.1 mL of DEET in 100 mL of ultrapure water, resulting in a concentration of 1000 mg/L, with a pH in the range of 6.9 to 7.0.
nodes.paragraph: This study evaluates the impacts of DEET on the biochemical composition of Chlorella vulgaris post-treatment to understand the phy - coremediation potential of the algal species relative to its tolerance limit. Ricky et al. Environmental Sciences Europe (2025) 37:36 Materials and methods Preparation of DEET stock solution N,N-Diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET) (CAS No: 134-62-3) stock solution (1000 mg/L) was prepared by dissolving 0.1 mL of DEET in 100 mL ultrapure water, and the pH of the stock solution was in the range of 6.9 7.0 consist - ent with the pH of ultrapure water. Working standards required for the test conditions were prepared by serial dilution of the stock solution and kept below 4 C in a dark, enclosed environment. The HPLC eluent prepara - tions employed acetonitrile of HPLC grade. Algae culture incubation conditions and batch experimentation Chlorella vulgaris (BDU GD003) seed cultures were pro - cured from the National Repository for Microalgae and Cyanobacteria-Freshwater, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, India. The algae were sub-cultured for 21 days in an orbital shaking incubator to attain stationary phase from seed culture with a fluorescent light intensity of 2000 Ix (12 h light/12 h dark cycle), and the culture was sub-cul - tured in BG-11 medium at 30 C. The experimental setup conditions were identical to prior investigations [23].

nodes.question: What is the purpose of homogenizing A. thaliana leaves in a homogenization buffer?
nodes.answer: The purpose of homogenizing A. thaliana leaves in a homogenization buffer is to extract proteins for further analysis.
nodes.paragraph: For the green surface area of the plant, this parameter represents the total area of the green parts of the leaves. In the ImageJ analysis, it was calculated using a fixed saturation range of 50 to 110, which specifically isolates the actively photosynthetic tissue. This range ensures that only the green, functional leaf areas are included in the measurement. A reduction in green surface area is an indicator of the CEO effect on the plant S ability to photosynthesize, reflecting damage to the chlorophyll-containing tissues. Protein extraction A. thaliana was chosen as a model plant because the full genome information was already available. For each sample, fresh matter from A. thaliana leaves was homogenized in a Potter homogenizer (Wheaton, IL, United States) in 800 mL of homogenization buffer (8 M urea, 100 mM TEAB (triethylammonium bicarbonate), pH 8.5 (HCI), 2 mM EDTA, 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), protease inhibitor mix composed of 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF, Merck-Sigma-Aldrich, Darmstadt, Germany), 2 g/mL each of leupeptin (Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany), aprotinin (Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany), antipain (Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany), pepstatin (Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany), and chymostatin (Merck-Sigma-Aldrich, Darmstadt, Germany), and 0.6% w/v polyvinylpolypyrrolidone (Polyclar AT, SERV A Electrophoresis GmbH, Heidelberg, Germany).

nodes.question: What are some components of the homogenization buffer used for protein extraction from A. thaliana leaves?
nodes.answer: The homogenization buffer contains 8 M urea, 100 mM TEAB, 2 mM EDTA, 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), and a protease inhibitor mix including phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF) and leupeptin, among others.
nodes.paragraph: For the green surface area of the plant, this parameter represents the total area of the green parts of the leaves. Protein extraction A. thaliana was chosen as a model plant because the full genome information was already available. nodes.question: How were the aquafaba samples prepared for use in the gluten-free cake production?
nodes.answer: The aquafaba samples were drained from the seeds of commercially canned pulses and then stored at 4°C before use.
nodes.paragraph: Using aquafaba in gluten-free cakes accelerated the starch stal- ing process, regarding staling kinetic parameters fitted to the Avrami model (n = 1). The consumption of control cake made with whole-eggs was not recommended after 7 days of storage at room temperature due to microbiological safety concerns whereas ESGF cakes could be consumed after 14 days of storage. * Gamze Nil Yazici gnboran@cu.edu.tr 1 Department of Food Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Cukurova University, Saricam, Balcali, 1330 Adana, Turkey 2 Department of Biostatistics, Faculty of Medicine, Cukurova University, Adana, Turkey G. N. Yazici et al. Graphical abstract Keywords Egg-free cake Thermal properties Crystallinity structure Retrogradation Shelf-life Introduction The food production must increase by approximately 60% by 2050 to satisfy the demand of the increasing world popula- tion [1 ]. However, it is estimated that nearly one-third of food is wasted or lost every year, according to FAO [2 ]. Therefore, food waste and/or loss is becoming one of the global problems, and so is at the center of sustainable devel - opment goals (SDG 2- Zero hunger , SDG 12- Respon- sible consumption and production , SDG 13- Climate action ), according to International Institute for Sustain- able Development [3 ].

nodes.question: How was the aquafaba prepared before being mixed into the ESGF cake batter?
nodes.answer: The aquafaba was drained from the seeds of commercially canned pulses and then stored at 4°C before mixing it into the cake batter.
nodes.paragraph: The whole eggs were replaced by an equal volumetric amount of aquafaba samples to produce ESGF cakes. The concentrations of all other cake ingredients remained constant. The flow dia- gram detailing the gluten-free cake formulation and pro - duction was illustrated in Fig. S1. To prepare the ESGF cake batter, firstly, aquafaba was mixed for 4 min at level 8 followed by 4 min at level 10 by using the Kitchen Aid Professional mixer KPM5 (St. Joseph, Michigan, USA). After the addition of sugar for 2 min at level 10, all dry ingredients (rice flour, xanthan gum, baking powder, vanil- lin, and salt) were sifted and weighed into a steel bowl, and the mixing process was continued thoroughly for 2 min at level 10. GF cake batter samples (50 0.5 g) were placed into silicon muffin moulds (90 mm diameter 33 mm height) and baked in a convection oven (EBO 1-64R, Wiesheu Wolfen GmBH, Wolfen, Germany) for 60 min at 180 . The baking parameters were decided according to ESGF and kept constant for the control cake for better comparison.
